card.name: Verbal nouns before "of"
card.fires_on: An -ing verb form used as a noun, right after "the", "a" or "no", usually followed by "of" or "back". It appears in literary or essay-style web prose, such as "the passing of" or "the dawning of".

modes.label: The -ing of
modes.description: An -ing noun after "the" that is followed by "of" and names an event or process.
modes.example: seem to toll The<< passing>> of the sweetest soul That ever

modes.label: Split -ing words
modes.description: The -ing ending of a word broken into pieces, such as fl-itting, d-awning or do-ings.
modes.example: Then there was a fl<<itting>> of those families. Some of them made

modes.label: No going back
modes.description: An -ing form after "no" or "a-" in a fixed phrase.
modes.example: seemed to believe that there was no<< going>> back. Others,
